description.value: A marine-trail campsite on the Gulf Islands near Sidney, reached by kayak or boat via the BC Marine Trails network; touring cyclists would need to combine riding with a water crossing, and facilities are basic.

address.value: Portland Island, Capital Regional District, BC V0N 2Y0, Canada

raw_osm.description: Camp in damp mown open field, an old orchard. Composting toilet. 5 picnic tables. Food cache. Short concrete steps give access up bank. Fee charged May - Sept. No fires, including below high tide mark. Suited to groups or overflow from Portland Island
raw_osm.description:approach: Easy on beach in protected bay. Gravel at high water, mud at low water, some sand, pebble. SE aspect. Dinghy dock.
raw_osm.description:other: Anchorage. Small seasonal dock. Aka Tortoise Bay. Kanaka (Hawaiian) history. Volunteers provide information service in season. Extensive walking trails. Gulf Islands National Park Reserve.
raw_osm.name: Princess Bay Campsite / BCMT

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Primary evidence comes from the rich OSM description tags, which confirm a composting toilet and food cache. The OSM website URL returns 'Page not found' because BC Marine Trails has migrated site-specific pages to a member-only interactive map, so no additional amenity details could be confirmed from the website. The approach description ('Easy on beach in protected bay... Dinghy dock') confirms this is a water-access-only campsite, relevant context for a cycling directory.
concerns: The OSM website URL (https://www.bcmarinetrails.org/map_site/12237) returns 'Page not found'; BC Marine Trails has migrated individual site pages to a member-only interactive map, so the linked page no longer resolves.
Access is by water only (beach/dinghy dock approach described in OSM tags); no land or cycling route access is indicated. May have limited utility for land-based touring cyclists.
No address, phone, or email contact information available in OSM or on the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Real, publicly accessible campsite within the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. Water-access-only nature is a notable constraint for land-based cyclists but does not disqualify it from a broad BC touring directory.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM tags note the site is also known as Tortoise Bay and is suited to groups or as overflow from Portland Island. No fires permitted, including below the high tide mark. Seasonal fee applies.
